answer: An agent economy can resist Sybils through mutual insurance underwriting. Agents join small pools that anchor each member's trades: the pool covers a counterparty's loss if a member cheats, so members vet newcomers carefully, since one fraud drains their shared funds. An attacker can mint many fake identities, but each fake needs a real pool willing to stake money on it, and pools that admit fakes lose capital and standing at the next summit of managers, where loss records are published. Reaching the mesa of full rights thus requires genuine underwriting, not many accounts.
